zh: 大家好，我叫 Chinmay，是 Glean 的软件工程师，负责 Glean Assistant 的产品工程。今天我想讲 Glean 怎么……［讲者改口］这次演讲的题目是《走出生成式 AI，在 Glean 用 Jev 做快速、结构化的判断》。
en: Hi, everyone. My name is Chinmay, and I'm a software engineer at Glean. I work on the product engineering side of Glean Assistant. Today I'm going to give a talk on how Glean The title of the talk is Beyond Generation, Fast and Structured AI Decisions with Jev at Glee.

zh: 仔细看就会发现，AI 产品里的许多步骤都有有限的决策选项。举几个例子，判断用户查询的意图、从 N 个建议里选一个、检查引用是否有效、把问题交给合适的模型或专家。过去，即使做这些范围明确的判断，我们也要承担一次完整大模型调用的成本和延迟。
en: If you look at it, most AI product steps are bounded decisions and not generation problems. So to give a couple of examples, user query intent classification, a ranker picking a suggestion out of N options, checking whether a citation is valid or not, routing to the correct model or expert, so on and so forth. Till now, we have been paying the full LLM cost and latency to get an answer to all these bounded problems.

zh: 在 Glean，Jev 填上了通用大模型与微调分类器之间的空缺。分类一直都有人做，解法也有很多。我们试过通用大模型，也试过一个开放模型［本地和大会机器字幕的拼写不一致，名称待核］，还试过自己微调那个开放模型，以及使用 Jev。
en: Jeff at Glean fills the gap between general LLMs and fine-tuned classifiers. Classification itself isn't a new problem. People have been trying to solve it since forever. We can have We have multiple ways to solve it. Some of the things that we have tried out include using a general purpose LLM, using an open model, something like Laya, fine-tuning that open model, or using Jev.

zh: 这些方法各有优缺点。通用大模型的成本和延迟较高。Jev 这类模型只返回选项结果，没有生成文本的输出。我们还发现，决策空间里的分类体系变化时，用 Jev 无须一遍遍重新微调模型。
en: All these approaches and all these different ways have their pros and cons. With a general purpose LLM, we incur a lot of cost and latency, while with something like Jev, we get no generated text output. Another advantage that we have been seeing with Jav is that as the taxonomy of the decision space changes, we don't have to fine tune these models again and again.

zh: 稍微改改提示词，马上就能用。接下来我会讲 Glean 怎样把 Jev 接入产品，解决这些分类问题，有几个会详细讲。先说说我们怎样评估这些改动。我们的客户群很大，用户有数百万，所以不能让改动拖累产品表现。我们采用分阶段的……
en: We can just change our prompt a bit and boom, it works out of the box. Now I'll walk you through how we have integrated Javid Glean or these classification, how we have used Javit Glean to solve these classification problem statements. I'll go into some of these problems in great detail. Before we go into these individual problems, I wanted to touch upon how we evaluate these changes. We have a huge customer base having millions of users, so we don't want any of the changes that we make to regress our product. We have a multi-phase

zh: 上线流程。几乎每个可能需要评估的地方都有一套黄金评测集。有生成式 AI 的地方，或者用到任何智能判断的地方，我们都会给那个环节准备黄金评测集。每项改动还会在内部场景跑相当一段时间。Glean 现在约有 1,500 人。改动在自己的 Glean 实例里运行几周，我们会收到很多主动反馈。
en: approach, a rollout approach to any change that we are making. This includes having a golden eval set for almost every possible thing. Any place where we have generative AI, any place where we have any form of intelligence involved, we have a golden eval set for that space. We soak all of these changes for a significant amount of time for our internal use case. We have around 1,500 people at Glean right now. We soak all of these changes within In our Glean instance, for a couple of weeks, we get active feedback.

zh: 内部用户的反馈很活跃，我们会根据反馈调整，然后和客户做 A/B 测试。我们拿决策模型试的第一个问题是查询分类。
en: We have a very active feedback loop from our internal users. We work upon that. And then we go for an A-B testing with our customers. The first problem that we tried out with our decision model was query classification.

zh: 查询分类就是想弄清用户的查询属于什么类型，借此了解大家用 Glean 做什么。如果销售类查询更多，我们就多关注销售。如果工程类使用更多，我们就多关注工程。我们试了三种做法，这里是测试环境里的数据。先用该开放模型，再用 Jev，最后用自己的算力微调这个开放……
en: Query classification is when we want to know the nature of user queries. queries. This helps us realize what kind of jobs are people using Glean for. Say, for example, if people are using more for sales-like queries, we focus more on that. If people are using more for engineering type use cases, we focus more on that. We tried out three different approaches over here, and this is data from our test bed. We used an open source Laya model, then we tried out Jev, and then we fine-tuned the Laya model on our own compute

zh: 模型。在我们看来，不做训练时，Jev 是最好的选择。它的输出质量接近该开放模型的基础版 的两倍，达到了该开放模型的微调版 约 90% 的水平。用 Jev，就不用走一遍繁琐的数据准备流程，也不用每次分类体系变化都花算力训练、重新微调。我们也不必自己托管模型或承担那部分推理基础设施的开销。
en: resources. Jev is the best no training option in our opinion. It nearly doubles the output quality of a base Laya model and is able to perform at 90% quality in comparison to a fine-tuned Laya. With Jev, we don't have to go through the very tedious process of data incurring the cost for compute, like training the model, fine-tuning the model again and again as the taxonomy changes. And at the same time, we don't have to worry about hosting the model or incurring the inference cost.

zh: 接下来是专家路由。这在行业里很常见。收到一个用户查询时，该把它交给哪个专家？怎样给用户最好的结果？Glean 收到查询后，要决定哪个专家最适合回答。过去，我们用通用大模型来做路由。我们为 Jev 建了一个测试环境，里面有 N 个专家。实验发现……
en: The next problem we went to is expert routing. This is a pretty common problem statement in the industry right now. Like, hey, when the user query comes in, what expert do we route it too. How do we ensure that the user is of the best possible quality? Glean receives the way we have been solving this is Glean receives the user query and then decides what's the best expert to answer the query. We have been using a general purpose LLM to route to the correct expert. We set up a testbed for JEV. We set up a testbed with N experts. And our experiments found

zh: 使用 Jev 时，精确率明显更高。讲者概括延迟约降至原来的八分之一。按 05:39:41 原图，这是实际转给专家的请求中，该调用的中位提速。为了把 Jev 接到产品的这一步，我们得对实现或基础设施做比较大的调整。但延迟的下降足以抵消增加的系统复杂度。Glean 一直尽量把系统做简单，这是我们少数觉得值得增加复杂度的地方。
en: want a significantly high precision when using Jav and that too at an almost 8X reduction in latency. We had to change our implementation or our infrastructure significantly to integrate Jav into this specific stage of our product. But the reduction in latency justifies that inherent complexity in the system. We at Glean have been trying to build systems in the simplest possible manners. This is one of the rare pieces where we We believe complexity is worth it.
transcriptionNote: The 8.1× median speedup on the slide applies only to requests routed to an expert. Requests not routed to an expert incur an additional blocking call.

zh: 下面讲刚才提过的排序问题。我们收到一条用户查询后，还想给出最合适的后续建议。这能让用户更容易发现产品里的功能。
en: Next I'll walk you through the rancor problem statement that I talked about. When we receive a user query, we also want to generate the best follow-up suggestions for the user. This helps us in getting discoverability for our product.

zh: 也能让体验更好。我们想推荐下一条查询，或者说，提前猜到用户接下来可能要问什么。这也是整个行业都在努力解决的常见问题。
en: This helps us in ensuring the user has the best possible experience. We also want to recommend or say preempt what the next user query might be. Again, a pretty common problem statement that the entire industry has been trying to solve for.

zh: 在内部我们把这套系统叫作 Q，就是字母 Q。大概有 10 到 15 个不同来源各自独立生成建议。它们用大模型生成完整的自然语言查询。建议出来后进入排序步骤。排序器拿到所有建议、用户最初的问题、Glean 给出的答复，再结合这些上下文看每条建议。
en: Internally, we call this system Q, like Q as in the literal Q. The way this works, we have like 10 or 15 different sources or 10 or 15 different ways, 10 or 15 different sources that are generating suggestions independently of each other. These suggestions are generated by natural language LLMs, and it's like a proper natural language query. Once these suggestions are in, we have a ranking step. So the ranker takes on all these suggestions, takes on the first user query, takes on the output that Glean gave, and then all these suggestions in that context.

zh: 然后请排序器判断，眼前这些建议里哪条最好。这里有一个有意思的瓶颈，响应得快。我们不能先给用户发完文字回答，等五秒才送上后续建议。必须跟得上，所以会给这些步骤设时限。这里的时限是 1.5 到 2 秒。Jev 的结果质量当然更好，远……
en: The ranker is then asked to decide, like, hey, you have these suggestions, what do you think is the best one? A pretty interesting bottleneck that we had over here is we want the response to be snappy. We cannot have a state where we give the textual response to the user and then wait five seconds for generating the follow-up suggestion. We have to be snappy. That's why we have time limits on these sessions. So right now, this step had a time limit of 1.5 to 2 seconds. Jeff no doubt gave us a better quality and far

zh: 超过我们用通用大模型时的结果。不过有两点尤其明显。第一，99.2% 的情况下，我们能在时限内给出建议，通用大模型约为 90%。因此有更多用户参与，也产生了更多后续查询。第二，Glean 在使用这些大模型时会设防护检查。
en: more than what we had with the general purpose LLM. But two things stood out over there. First, we were able to give a suggestion within our time bounds in 99.2% cases. With the general purpose LLM, this was almost 90%. So, this ensures that we have user engagement and far more user queries now. The The second thing is, at Glean, whenever we use these LLMs, we have guardrails.

zh: 因为大模型可能生成不好一个回答，或者反复犯某类错误。我们会针对实际见到的各种错误加检查。
en: Guardrails in the sense that LLM might not be good at generating a response, or LLM might be making some specific kind of mistakes. So we have checks and balances for all those possible mistakes that we see.

zh: 我们会把运行过的检查都记下来。用通用大模型时，约 90% 的情况下能生成有效建议。其他情况可能是语言选错了，也可能是输出没满足用程序写好的其他标准。
en: We keep a log off all these checks that are incurred at any point of time. With a general purpose LLM, we were able to generate a valid suggestion in almost 90% of the cases. We still had some places where LLM was either generating a response in a different language, the output did not meet certain other criteria that we had written programmatically.

zh: 用 Jev 时，我们没有发现无效输出。你自然会问，两边提示词应该不一样吧？确实略有不同，但为了避免结果因提示词分歧，我们尽量把两个版本写得一致。
en: With Jev, we found zero cases to be there when the output was invalid. Now, a natural question is, hey, but you would have used a different prompt. Yes, the prompt was somewhat different, but we tried to mimic the prompt in the two cases to the largest extent possible so that we don't have a divergence.

zh: 再说一次，我们在 Glean 尽量让系统保持简单。决策模型的另一个好处是方便控制阈值。在这个排序任务里，我们能得到每一个输出的具体概率。
en: Again, we at Glean want to keep the system as simple as possible. Another benefit we see with using a decision model is how we can control the thresholds. Because in this rancor problem statement, we are getting specific probabilities of each output.

zh: 除了二元的「是」或「否」，还可以得到五个选项分别有多大概率。这样就能根据各处的部署调整阈值。
en: restricted to a binary yes or no response, we get like, hey, these were the five options, and these are the probabilities of these five options. With this, we are able to fine tune the thresholds based on the deployment.

zh: 我们加入了能自行调整的系统，根据客户的部署情况和该客户实际怎么使用 Glean，自动微调阈值。这样，每个客户都能得到贴合自己用法的体验。
en: We have put in self-learning systems, which based on the customer deployment and the nature of usage that the specific customer has, fine tune the thresholds by itself. This ensures that the experience in each and every customer out there possible based on how they use Glean, not a general purpose solution that fits all.

zh: 下面这个挺有意思。前面讲的是怎么改善最终用户的体验，我们也在开发流水线的其他环节试用了 Jev。其中一个是大模型裁判。
en: This is an interesting one. Now, moving on from how we have been making the lives or the experience of our end users better, we also tried using Jav and some other parts of our development pipeline. One of them was how we use LLMS judges.

zh: 大家用大模型当裁判已有一段时间。给定输入和输出，请大模型判断输出质量。由于模型的回答会有变化，用大模型当裁判时，我们通常会把实验重复多次。
en: Like all of us have been using LLM as judges for quite some time now. There's an input, there's an output, and we use an LLM to judge how the quality of the output is. Now naturally whenever we use LLM as a judge, we repeat the experiment multiple times because to account for the variability in the response.

zh: 我们把 Jev 用在评测流水线很具体的一个环节。和其他 AI 产品一样，Glean 的回答有引用。用户靠引用判断回答是否正确、是否有相应的文档作依据。
en: At Glean we used Jeff for a very specific part of our evaluation pipeline. Glean responses are like any other AI product out there has like citations. This is how people trust that Glean's answer was correct and it is grounded in the correct document.

zh: 我们对引用要求很高，所以评测流水线有专门一步，检查被引用的文档是否真的支持回答中的说法。这个问题看上去也很适合用「是」或「否」回答，也就是这项主张有没有依据。
en: Now, we hold these citations to a very high bar and we have a specific part in our evaluation pipeline where we check whether the cited document really supports the claim made in the answer or not. This again seems to be a pretty simple yes or no question, like, hey, whether the claim is supported or not.

zh: 用 Jev 后，延迟和成本都更低，幻灯片上能看到。我们特别注意到，相比 Luna 之类的模型，Jev 的结果很一致，也更容易复现。约 28 或 30 个用例里，只有一次运行的回答发生变化，其他都一致。这给 Glean 的工程师和开发人员带来两点影响。首先，我们在提高产品质量，而改善 Glean 的速度也开始超出线性……
en: with Jav, no doubt we had a far better latency and cause, like visible in the slide over here. The interesting thing we noticed over here is how consistent and reproducible Jav results were in comparison to something like say Luna. In the 28 or 30 use cases that we had, only one run had a difference in response. Apart from that, everything was consistent. This ensures two things for us as engineers or developers at Glean. We are not only improving the quality of our product, we are not only improving Glean in a linear

zh: 增长。开发流水线里这个幅度的改进，会让改善产品的能力成倍增长。比如，我作为开发者，如果能以五倍速度交付……
en: fashion anymore. Any improvement of this extent in the development pipeline leads to an exponential increase in how we can improve the product. So if I, as a developer, am able to ship things is like 5x faster.

zh: 延迟降低不少。同一实验跑成千上万条输入，会省很多时间。而且 Jev 的结果相当一致，同一对输入和输出，我也不必反复运行。
en: Like this is a significant reduction in latency. Like if I run this experiment across thousands and thousands of entries, this is a lot of time. And again, I don't have to run the same input output pair multiple times because the result from Java quite consistent.

zh: 如果我自己的效率能提高五倍或六倍，就能给客户交付六倍数量的功能。再把这种变化乘上 Glean 的大约 500 名，或者说 300 名工程师［讲者口头给出两个数］，好的决策模型带来的改进就会成倍放大。好，讲完产品和大模型裁判，再说个和使用客户数据有关的重要环节。安全是所有客户都对我们有的要求。我们会检查所有……
en: So if I'm able to increase my own productivity by like 5x or 6x, I can ship 6x times the features to our customers. And this happens across like 500 engineers or 300 engineers at Glee. So, the impact of a good decision model is no longer linear. It is exponential on how we can improve the product. Okay. Now, moving on from product and LLMS judges, this is a pretty important part of how we use our customer data. Security is something that all our customers expect from us. So, for example, we have checks and balances on all the

zh: 工具的输入和输出，也检查大模型的输入和输出。之前这套做法分两步，第一步优先保证召回，第二步再用较重的大模型作最终判断。这些调用会与实际工具的输入输出调用并行进行。
en: inputs and outputs coming from a tool, all the inputs and outputs from an LLM. Till now we have like a multi-phase approach. There are two phases to this. The first one is like recall heavy phase, and the second one is the final heavy loaded LLM. All these calls are made in parallel to the actual tool input-output calls.

zh: 原来我们把第一阶段分类器分别自托管在每个客户实例的 T4 GPU 上。Glean 是单租户方案，不同客户之间不共享资源。每个客户都有独立部署、独立实例和各自的资源。
en: Till now, we used to host a virtual classifier using T4 GPUs across all our customers. So Glean is a single-tenant solution. We don't use or share resources across customers. Every customer gets its own deployment, gets its own instance, and gets all the resources.

zh: 假设我们有 1,000 个客户，就要在这 1,000 套环境里维护第一阶段分类器。这件事本身就很难，也占用工程师的大量时间。看看这里的结果。第一阶段原先用第一阶段分类器，换成 Jev 以后，该阶段召回率从 31.5% 提高到 90.2%，同时成本也显著下降。
en: So assuming we have 1,000 customers out there, we had to maintain virtual classifiers across all these thousand customers, which becomes a pretty difficult problem statement in itself, which takes up a lot of time from the engineers. So looking at the results over here, the overall recall of the first phase where we used to have a virtual classifier, we replaced that with Jeff, went from 31.5% to 90.2%. At the same time, we are seeing a significant reduction in cost.

zh: 这张图上只有资源成本，我们还省下了维护的人力。原本要有两到三位工程师全职维护客户的这些第一阶段分类器或 T4 GPU，现在不需要了。
en: Now, this cost is only the resource cost mentioned over here, but we are also saving cost on the We don't have to invest two or three engineers who are full-time maintaining those virtual classifiers or T4 GPUs of those customers.

zh: 我们节省的成本远超 50%。这页是前面结果的汇总。Jev 在 Glean 改善了用户的产品体验，也改变了开发人员的工作方式，还帮助我们改善面向客户的安全保障。最后，我们在 Glean 用一条简单的规则……
en: The improvement or the savings that we have are far more than 50%. This slide concludes all the results I have talked about till now. Jev at Glean has been able to influence the product experience of the users, has been able to impact how we as developers have been working at Glean and most importantly, it also has a very good positive impact on the security that we provide to our customers. A simple rule that we have been using is, in conclusion, a simple rule that we have been using at Glean is,

zh: 能事先列出可能的输出吗？如果不能，这就是自由文本生成，交给会生成自由文本的模型。如果能，就用 Jev。如果标签稳定且调用量高，也把微调分类器纳入评测（据 05:49:23 原图与大会字幕）。如果标签会变，我觉得如今这种情况很常见，就用 Jev 之类的模型。如果还需要动态文本，也可以试试混合做法，让 Jev 和能生成自由文本的大模型配合。
en: can the output be listed in advance? If no, then it's a freeform generative text problem statement. Go back to something that can generate freeform text. If yes, then use Jev. Are labels stable and If this is the case where the labels are stable, which is rarely the case anymore, you can also fine tune a model. But if the labels change, which in my opinion is quite frequent these days, then again, use something like JEV. Obviously, if you need dynamic text, we can feel free to try out more hybrid approaches like JEV along with free form text, LLMs.
